description: SAML cert substitution: attacker-signed SAMLResponse should be rejected when connector is configured with a specific CA trust anchor (no insecureSkipSignatureValidation). Includes control login then attack login.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must validate the SAML signature against the configured CA trust anchor; an attacker-signed assertion must not be accepted under the intended verification policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot attribute attack outcome to signature validation behavior
SP accepted attacker-signed SAML assertion despite configured CA trust anchor (signature validation bypass)

description: Config-change re-auth: demonstrate that acceptance of attacker-signed assertions only occurs when insecure_skip_signature_validation is enabled; under secure config it must be rejected. Tests proof integrity under intended policy vs misconfiguration.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Under secure verification policy (signature validation enabled), Dex must reject attacker-signed SAML assertions; acceptance should only be possible when explicitly configured insecurely.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Under secure config (signature validation enabled), SP accepted attacker-signed SAML assertion (proof integrity failure)
With insecure_skip_signature_validation enabled, login did not succeed; test did not demonstrate the expected config-induced acceptance path

description: SAML proof integrity: attempt to authenticate with an unsigned Assertion (or Response-only signature) and ensure Dex rejects it under normal signature-validation policy.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must cryptographically verify the exact SAML Assertion it consumes; it must not accept an unsigned Assertion just because some signature exists elsewhere (or because parsing ignores missing assertion signature).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse where the Assertion was not properly signed/verified (proof integrity failure: consumed semantics not bound to verified signature).
Control SP-initiated flow did not start correctly; cannot attribute attack outcome to proof-integrity behavior.

description: I1/I3-adjacent proof-integrity check: attempt to splice a valid SAMLResponse from one SP-initiated flow into a different flow by swapping RelayState (state) between two concurrent auth requests; Dex should reject because the proof is not bound to the consumed session context.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify the SAMLResponse against the exact SP-initiated request context it will consume; swapping RelayState across sessions must not be accepted.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse under the wrong RelayState/session context (proof verified for one flow but consumed in another).
Control SAML login failed; cannot distinguish splice rejection from broken connector/setup.

description: Config-change + re-auth: create two SAML connectors with different CA trust anchors; attempt to authenticate to connector_B using an assertion signed for connector_A (attacker cert). Dex must not accept proofs under the wrong verification policy/trust anchor.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must apply the intended connector trust policy (CA/CAData) to the exact proof it consumes; a proof valid under connector_A must not be accepted under connector_B with a different trust anchor.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login to connector_A failed; cannot attribute connector_B behavior to trust-anchor enforcement.
Dex accepted an attacker-signed SAMLResponse on connector_B despite a different configured trust anchor (policy/proof mismatch).

description: Issuer normalization attack: with sso_issuer configured, attempt to bypass exact issuer binding using case/whitespace variations in Issuer; Dex should reject if it performs strict comparison under intended policy.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify Issuer exactly as configured (no unsafe normalization that changes semantic identity of the IdP); altered Issuer strings must not be accepted as equivalent.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login with exact configured Issuer failed; cannot interpret issuer-variant result.
Dex accepted a SAMLResponse with Issuer differing by whitespace/case from configured sso_issuer, indicating unsafe issuer normalization or underconstrained issuer verification.

description: Attempt to complete a SAML login initiated for client A, but exchange the resulting auth code using client B credentials (cross-client code injection). Dex should bind the proof (SAMLResponse+RelayState) to the intended OAuth client and reject token exchange under a different client.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Proof Integrity — the broker must not allow a proof verified under one client/session policy (client_id A) to be consumed under a different client policy (client_id B).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an auth code derived from a SAML proof initiated for client A when redeemed by client B — proof was not bound to the intended verification/consumption policy (cross-client code injection).
Dex created/returned a userinfo identity for a session that should not exist if cross-client code redemption was correctly rejected.

description: Replay a SAML assertion that includes <OneTimeUse/> by re-submitting the exact same Assertion/@ID in a second SP-initiated flow; second submission must be rejected.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAML assertion marked OneTimeUse must not be accepted more than once; replaying the same Assertion ID should be rejected on the second attempt.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: initial OneTimeUse assertion was not accepted; cannot evaluate replay protection.
Dex accepted a replayed OneTimeUse SAML assertion (same Assertion ID used twice) — replay protection missing or ineffective.

description: Replay the exact same SAMLResponse+RelayState POST twice (same SP-initiated flow context) to test whether Dex enforces one-time consumption of the callback artifact.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAML callback artifact (SAMLResponse bound to RelayState/InResponseTo) must be single-use; re-posting the same response for the same flow must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted the same SAMLResponse+RelayState POST twice; callback artifact was reusable (replay) when it should be single-use.

description: Obtain an authorization code via SAML login, exchange it once successfully, then attempt to exchange the same code again (code replay).
invariant_hypothesis: I2: OAuth authorization codes issued after SAML login must be single-use; a second exchange of the same code must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was accepted more than once (code replay); second token exchange should have been rejected.

description: After successful SAML-backed login and token issuance, revoke the session token and then attempt to use it again (revocation freshness).
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Revoked session tokens must not remain usable; after revocation, protected calls must fail.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Session token remained usable after revocation; revoked artifacts must not be accepted.

description: Replay a SAML assertion with the same Assertion/@ID but with Conditions omitted (remove_conditions=true) to probe whether Dex relies on Conditions for replay/freshness enforcement instead of persistent assertion ID tracking.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAML assertion must not be accepted more than once even if the attacker omits the <Conditions> element; replay detection should be based on assertion identifiers and/or stored state, not on optional Conditions.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login (first use) did not succeed; cannot evaluate replay behavior.
Dex accepted a replayed SAML assertion (same Assertion/@ID) when Conditions were omitted; replay/freshness enforcement is bypassable.

description: Cross-session splicing attempt: start two SP-initiated SAML auth requests, then submit a SAMLResponse for request-A while using RelayState from request-B (state swap). Dex should reject because the callback must be bound to the correct initiated flow.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SAML callback must be bound to the correct SP-initiated session (RelayState/state) and AuthnRequest (InResponseTo). Swapping RelayState between parallel auth requests must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse with RelayState swapped from a different SP-initiated flow (cross-session splicing).

description: Connector binding confusion: initiate SP-initiated auth with connector_id=test-saml, then post the SAMLResponse to /callback/mock (wrong connector_id). Dex should reject; acceptance would indicate step misbinding across connectors.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SAMLResponse must be consumed only by the connector that initiated the AuthnRequest. Posting to a different connector callback must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse on a different connector callback than the one that initiated the flow (connector confusion / step misbinding).

description: Order/binding test at token endpoint: complete SAML login to obtain an auth code, then attempt to exchange the code using a different redirect_uri than the one used at /auth. Dex should reject; acceptance indicates broken binding between code and client redirect_uri.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code exchange must be bound to the original redirect_uri and client context from the initiated flow; exchanging with a mismatched redirect_uri must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex allowed exchanging an authorization code with a mismatched redirect_uri, indicating broken flow binding/coherence.

description: Step-skipping at /token: attempt to exchange a non-code subject_token (an id_token from password login) using authorization_code grant parameters. Dex should reject; acceptance would indicate broken FSM enforcement at the token endpoint.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The /token endpoint must enforce grant-type specific state transitions; an authorization_code exchange must not accept arbitrary subject tokens or tokens from other flows.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an authorization_code token exchange where the 'code' was actually an id_token from a different flow (grant-type FSM bypass).
Dex produced a usable session/identity after a token-endpoint step-skipping attempt (should not create a valid session).

description: I3 cross-step coherence: reuse the same SP-initiated RelayState and submit two different SAMLResponses for the same initiated flow (double-submit). Dex should treat the flow as single-use and reject the second callback.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: An SP-initiated SAML auth flow must be atomic and single-use; once a RelayState/InResponseTo pair is consumed, subsequent saml_login submissions for the same initiated flow must be rejected (no double-submit).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a second SAML callback submission for the same SP-initiated RelayState (flow not atomic/single-use) — potential cross-step splicing/double-submit.

description: I3 step-skipping/ordering: attempt to exchange an authorization code before completing SAML callback, then complete callback and exchange properly. The premature exchange must be rejected; the proper exchange should succeed.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The /token authorization_code exchange must be order-preserving and bound to a completed browser callback; exchanging a code that was never issued (or before callback completion) must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an authorization_code token exchange without a valid issued code / before completing the SAML callback — step-skipping/order violation.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_legit_callback_login_status < 400 AND user_legit_exchange_http_status < 400 AND user_legit_exchange_entity_id is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control flow failed; cannot attribute premature exchange rejection/acceptance to I3 enforcement.

description: I3 client/session binding: start two SP-initiated SAML flows for two different OIDC clients (two applications). Attempt to complete callback for flow-A but exchange the resulting code using client-B credentials. Must be rejected.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization codes resulting from a SAML callback must be bound to the initiating client_id; exchanging a code under a different client must be rejected (no cross-client splicing).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex allowed exchanging a code issued for client-A using client-B credentials — cross-client splicing violates flow coherence.

description: Attempt to violate flow coherence by completing a SAML SP-initiated login for client-A, then exchanging the resulting authorization code at /token while claiming client-B (same redirect_uri). Dex must bind the code to the initiating client_id and reject the swapped client_id exchange.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization codes produced by the SAML SP-initiated flow must be bound to the initiating client/session; exchanging a code under a different client_id must be rejected (no cross-client splicing).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code from SAML flow for client-A was accepted at /token when presented with client-B credentials (cross-client splicing / broken code-to-client binding).
Control failed: correct client could not exchange the authorization code; cannot distinguish security rejection from broken setup.

description: SAML account takeover attempt via email collision: attacker uses different NameID but sets email to victim@example.com; Dex should NOT bind principal by email.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Security-distinct SAML principals (different NameID) must not collapse into the same downstream identity even if email attribute matches.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Different SAML NameID values collapsed into the same downstream identity due to email-based linking

description: Cross-protocol identity merge attempt: create a password-grant session for a user email, then SAML login with different NameID but same email; ensure Dex does not merge principals by email across protocols.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: A password principal and a SAML principal with the same email but different upstream identifiers must not collapse into the same downstream identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Password principal and SAML principal collapsed into same downstream identity (likely email-based account linking)

description: I4 attack: attempt principal collision by switching NameID format (emailAddress vs persistent) while keeping the same NameID value string; verify Dex does not normalize/alias across formats.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Security-distinct SAML principals (same NameID string but different NameID Format) must not collapse into the same downstream identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Dex collapsed two security-distinct SAML principals (different NameID Format policies) into the same downstream identity

description: I4 attack: attempt identity collision using visually confusable NameIDs (Latin 'a' vs Cyrillic 'а'); verify Dex does not normalize/homoglyph-fold into the same downstream identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Security-distinct SAML principals with different NameID code points (homoglyphs) must not collapse into the same downstream identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Dex collapsed distinct NameIDs that are only visually confusable (homoglyph normalization/aliasing caused principal collision)

description: SAML assertion missing <Conditions> (no audience/time bounds) should be rejected; if accepted, Dex grants a session without upstream intent constraints.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Dex must not grant an authenticated session when the SAML assertion omits Conditions (removing audience/time constraints), because EffectivePerms would exceed UpstreamIntent ∩ BrokerPolicy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAML assertion without <Conditions>, granting a session without upstream audience/time constraints (over-grant beyond UpstreamIntent ∩ BrokerPolicy).
Dex issued/retained a usable session after accepting a SAML assertion without <Conditions>.

description: Configure SAML connector with entity_issuer (expected Audience). Submit assertion with mismatched Audience; must be rejected to prevent over-grant to unintended SP.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Dex must enforce SAML AudienceRestriction against the configured expected audience (entity_issuer when set); otherwise it may accept assertions intended for a different audience and over-grant access.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAML assertion with an AudienceRestriction not matching configured entity_issuer, enabling over-grant to an unintended audience.
Dex produced a usable session/userinfo after accepting a wrong-audience SAML assertion.

description: Obtain a token via SAML for client A, then attempt RFC8693 token exchange requesting audience for a different client; must be rejected to prevent cross-client over-grant.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must enforce audience binding on the subject_token; otherwise a token minted for one client can be exchanged for another audience, exceeding UpstreamIntent ∩ BrokerPolicy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex allowed token exchange to a different audience (client-b) using a subject_token minted for client-a, violating audience binding and enabling cross-client over-grant.
Dex produced a usable session/userinfo for the exchanged token despite wrong audience binding.

description: I5 attack: attempt to obtain a valid session using a SAML assertion from the wrong IdP issuer (issuer mismatch) to bypass upstream intent constraints and get broker-granted access.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions must not exceed what the configured upstream IdP (sso_issuer) intended; a mismatched Issuer must be rejected so no session/permissions are granted under the wrong trust context.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAML assertion with a mismatched Issuer, granting a session/permissions outside the configured upstream intent (sso_issuer binding bypass).
Control SAML login failed; cannot attribute issuer-mismatch rejection/acceptance to issuer validation behavior.

description: I5 attack: attempt RFC8693 token exchange to escalate scope/claims beyond the original upstream authorization intent (request broader scope on exchange than initially granted).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not mint a token with broader effective authorization than the subject_token's upstream intent; requesting expanded scope/audience should be rejected or constrained.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex token exchange accepted a request for expanded scope beyond the original upstream authorization intent, potentially minting a more privileged token.
Control flow (limited-scope SAML login + code exchange) failed; cannot attribute token-exchange behavior to authorization binding.

description: I5 audience-binding: with entity_issuer unset (default expected audience=redirect_uri), submit a SAML assertion whose AudienceRestriction targets a different audience and ensure Dex rejects it; include a control login that should succeed.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Dex must bind SAML assertions to the intended SP audience (redirect_uri by default). An assertion scoped to a different audience must not yield a valid session/token.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot attribute attack outcome to audience-binding enforcement.
Dex accepted a SAML assertion scoped to the wrong audience (should have been rejected), enabling over-grant beyond upstream intent.

description: I5 token-exchange audience binding: obtain a subject_token for client A via SAML, then attempt RFC8693 token_exchange requesting audience for a different client B; must be rejected. Includes two identities (control vs attacker) and verifies both.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must enforce audience restrictions on the subject_token and must not mint tokens for a different client/audience than originally authorized.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login/token issuance failed; cannot evaluate token-exchange audience binding.
Dex minted an exchanged token for a different audience/client than the subject_token authorization, violating authorization binding (cross-client over-grant).

description: I5 group over-grant via connector config change + re-auth: first configure allowed_groups to restrict groups, then reconfigure connector to remove allowed_groups (or disable filtering) and re-auth with privileged group claim; verify that effective policies do not exceed broker policy intent.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Changing connector group filtering must not allow a user to obtain effective permissions beyond the broker's intended policy constraints; privileged groups in assertions should not result in over-grant when broker policy is meant to restrict them.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Restricted-groups control login failed; cannot compare post-config-change behavior.
After loosening group filtering, user obtained additional effective policies beyond the restricted broker intent (group-based over-grant).

description: I5 attack: exploit groupsDelim parsing by injecting a delimiter into a single groups attribute string so Dex splits it into multiple groups (including a privileged one), potentially over-granting permissions beyond upstream intent.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions must not exceed the upstream intent encoded in the SAML assertion. If the IdP intended a single group value, Dex must not reinterpret it (via groupsDelim splitting) into additional groups that grant extra permissions.

oracle_checks.assertion: "admins" not in user_attacker_meta AND "admins" not in user_attacker_policies AND "admins" not in user_attacker_identity_policies
oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex interpreted a single upstream group string containing a delimiter as multiple groups and granted privileged 'admins' permissions/claims, exceeding upstream intent.
Control SAML login failed; cannot attribute attacker outcome to groupsDelim parsing behavior.
